subject: Coverage lane consolidation — MSA markup and capacity term proposal
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Amir Patel <amir@heliosys.com>, procurement@heliosys.com
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Coverage lane consolidation — MSA markup and capacity term proposal

Hi Amir / Helio team,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Per our conversation I attached an annotated MSA ("heliosys_msa_annotated_v2.docx") that captures the coverage-lane consolidation you requested and a couple of suggested guardrails for surge capacity. Key points we flagged in the markup:

- Term: proposed 18 months with phased ramp (months 1–3 ramp at 50% of uplift capacity, full in month 4).
- Tier swap: consolidate three overlapping lanes into two tiers to simplify billing and SLAs.
- Escrow / continuity: small carve for escrow responsibilities during a term-change window — legal asked us to be explicit about data export timelines.
- Audit logs: we preserved the existing audit retention language but added a note on retention scope for deduped telemetry.

Can you review the annotated MSA and the two inline questions on Section 4.2 (surge billing) and Section 9.1 (termination transition)? If those look ok we can prepare the short amendment + updated order form for signature.

If it helps, happy to do a 30-min walkthrough with your legal + procurement tomorrow afternoon (I have 1–3pm PT open).

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment: heliosys_msa_annotated_v2.docx (docx)
From: Amir Patel <amir@heliosys.com>

Cc: Helio Systems Legal <legal@heliosys.com>, procurement@heliosys.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coverage lane consolidation — MSA markup and capacity term proposal

Soojin — thanks for the doc. We went through the markup with Legal & Procurement and attached our annotated order form ("Helio_OrderForm_markup.pdf"). Main open items from our side:

1) Term length — Legal prefers 12 months with an automatic renewal language rather than an 18-month fixed term. They are concerned about fiscal forecasting for Q1 next year.
2) Escrow clause — our counsel wants the escrow responsibilities to be reciprocal; they asked for a phrase that limits Redwood's obligations to the exported telemetry format we currently support.
3) Surge billing — Procurement asks for a cap on monthly surge charges (propose $100k/mo cap during a three-month trial).

I can join a call tomorrow at 2pm PT to walk through if that works.

Thanks,
Amir

Attachment: Helio_OrderForm_markup.pdf (pdf)

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Coverage lane consolidation — summarize external asks + internal proposal

Soojin / team — quick summary after Amir's note and our internal legal review:

External asks to address:
- Helio wants 12 months + auto-renew (vs our 18 months phased ramp)
- Reciprocal escrow phrasing requested by Helio legal
- Procurement wants an initial monthly surge cap for the trial period

Proposed internal posture (attached draft amendment "proposed_amendment_draft.docx"):
- Accept 12 months term but add an explicit phased ramp schedule as an Appendix A (gives them short-term flexibility while preserving uplift timelines).
- Escrow: offer a reciprocal escrow sentence but narrow the export format and timeline to 30 days post-termination (legal flagged export complexity beyond that window).
- Surge cap compromise: agree to a $75k/mo cap for the first 3 months of uplift, then revert to standard surge billing (we should quantify the expected token/day at that cap).

Ask: can Marcus confirm the cost math on the $75k cap (rough token estimate attached), and Jordan — if you agree, I'll send a consolidated reply to Amir with the amendment and a proposed DocuSign link. If procurement pushes back at 2pm PT call, we should be prepared to trade a slightly higher cap for a 15% up-front seat commitment.

Thanks,
Naomi

Attachment: proposed_amendment_draft.docx (docx)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Amir Patel <amir@heliosys.com>, Helio Systems Legal <legal@heliosys.com>, procurement@heliosys.com

Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coverage lane consolidation — MSA markup and capacity term proposal

Amir / Helio team — thanks for the quick turnaround on your markup and for joining the call today. We consolidated your feedback and propose the following path to close this week: 

1) Term & ramp: move to a 12-month MSA with Appendix A that documents a phased ramp (50% uplift months 1–3, full capacity month 4). Appendix A will be part of the amendment and is limited in scope to the pledge of uplift capacity.
2) Escrow: reciprocal escrow sentence accepted; we narrowed export obligations to the current telemetry export format and a 30-day fulfillment window.
3) Surge cap: agree to a $75k/month cap for months 1–3 as a compromise; after month 3 surge charges follow standard tier pricing. In lieu of a higher cap, we ask for a 15% seat commitment for the uplift period (to be captured in the order form).

Next steps: attached is a short term sheet ("term-sheet-v3.pdf") and a DocuSign link for the amendment/Appendix A. If you can confirm by EOD Monday we will route the amendment to Legal + Sales Ops for signature and schedule a billing cutover for the start of the uplift.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/link/3xY-Helio-TermSheet-V3
Drive folder with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-HelioRenewal

If any legal redlines remain, please send them back in tracked changes to the amendment doc; otherwise we'll proceed with the DocuSign flow.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
